channel.title: East & Inner with Ollie
channel.description: Classical Chinese medicine, translated for the modern ear. No jargon. No mysticism. Just the real stuff — from the Huangdi Neijing to your morning coffee. Hosted by Ollie, a screech owl with a yin-yang pendant and a lot of questions. New episodes every other week.
channel.itunes:author: Ollie
channel.itunes:summary: Classical Chinese medicine, translated for the modern ear. No jargon. No mysticism. Just the real stuff — from the Huangdi Neijing to your morning coffee.

item.title: Ep01: Yin & Yang ≠ Good vs Evil
item.description: The biggest mistranslation in the history of wellness culture: Yin and Yang are NOT good and evil. Ollie walks you through the seesaw, the three rules nobody told you, and why you should stop driving nails through your internal balance.
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep02: Stop Fighting, Start Warming
item.description: When a cold hits, your first instinct is to fight it. But Chinese medicine says that's exactly the wrong move. Discover the three warming herbs — Gui Zhi, Gan Jiang, and Fu Zi — and learn why your body doesn't need a warrior. It just needs a blanket.
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep03: Traffic Jam — Why Your Emotions Get Stuck
item.description: You're stuck. Irritable. Everything feels like too much. Classical Chinese medicine calls this Liver Qi stagnation — your internal traffic is gridlocked. Ollie explains the highway inside your body, why emotions really do get stuck, and what Xiao Yao San has been doing about it for a thousand years.
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep04: What Is Qi, Actually?
item.description: You've heard the word a thousand times. But what IS Qi, actually? Not the wellness-industry version — the real thing. Ollie explains the five functions of Qi, the four ways it goes wrong, and why your body has been trying to tell you something your whole life.
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep05: Food Temperature — Why Your Body Doesn't Want That Salad
item.description: Every wellness influencer tells you to eat more salads. But some bodies don't want cold food — they want warmth. Ollie explains the forgotten wisdom of food temperature, the digestive fire, and why Chinese medicine has been warning about cold foods for two thousand years.
item.itunes:author: Ollie
